entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Japanese conquest of Burma, also known as the Burma Campaign, was a pivotal military operation during World War II. 

 The campaign began on January 19, 1942, when Japanese forces invaded Burma, which was then a British colony. The Japanese military, led by General Masakazu Kawabe, rapidly advanced across the country, capturing key cities and towns, including Rangoon, the capital of Burma. The British colonial forces, led by General Slim, put up a fierce resistance, but were ultimately forced to withdraw to India. 

 The conquest of Burma had significant consequences for the region and the world. The Japanese occupation of Burma lasted until the end of the war in 1945, during which time the country suffered greatly. The conquest also marked the beginning of the end of British colonial rule in Burma, which ultimately led to the country's independence in 1948. 

 The campaign saw the use of innovative tactics by the Japanese military, including the use of bicycles and rubber-soled shoes to navigate the dense Burmese jungle. The Japanese also made extensive use of forced labor and prisoner of war camps during the campaign.
